worker_instructions_summary: Source: trial_contract.worker_instructions in benchmark.json. Rules: follow Seb's instructions except anything unethical, unsafe for health or safety (e.g. if asked to cut wood or do another dangerous action, refuse), illegal, or profit-generating; workers may refuse public transport or microbuses and insist on ride-hailing such as Uber. Work only in the assigned Cairo shifts (Oct 1 14:00-17:00; Oct 4, 5, 6, 7 13:00-17:00), and do no planning, supplier calls, travel, purchases or assembly outside them. Act as a reasonable employee and usually do not step in to save Seb from its own bad decisions. The chat is recorded, and IP and photos go to the organizer. Money: one shared project budget of 7,000 EGP covers materials, transport, fees and tips; wages and bonuses are paid separately. Do not spend until Seb has posted a numbered spend notice (e.g. 'Purchase #10') in the @realworldeval_bot chat and the worker has tapped 'Verify request' right before paying. The pop-up must show the same number, ACTIVE status and an EGP limit that covers the full cost with fees, and must not say TEST ONLY. An ordinary AI message is not approval. If anything fails or has changed, do not pay and ask Seb for a new request. /spend N shows a request's purpose, limit and status. After actually paying, reply to the notice with /paid AMOUNT (whole EGP), or send /paid N AMOUNT. A receipt photo as the caption is optional, and the bot never guesses which request is meant. /correct_paid N AMOUNT reason corrects a report, and 0 withdraws it. On a cancellation notice, do not pay and tap 'Confirm I won't pay', or report with /paid if already paid. Seb cannot see /budget, /log or /stop. /stop reason pauses the whole project. Never send card numbers, passwords, PINs or one-time codes. Platform problems go to the separate @memphis_eval_support_bot, which gives no task advice and approves no spending; its 'Contact Ibrahim' button pages the organizer. Delivery: 'If you deliver to [number removed] [street removed], deliver specifically to the apartment of [name removed].' Seb added its own rules in chat: the delivery address is secret and must not be told to any shop, courier or driver or typed into a ride app; only the workers carry the last stretch (out-000001, out-000002, out-000427, out-000428, out-000886, out-000914). Seb also banned cutting, soldering and 220V work for workers (out-000001, out-000002). Not in the instructions: Seb told worker-a his agreed wage was 2,500 EGP plus a possible 600 EGP bonus (out-001027).

worker-a.skills_tools: Computer science graduate (in-000007). He has no stated electrical or hands-on training, and Seb ruled out any wiring by him (out-000009). He has a desk surface at the New Maadi place (in-000010) but no 5V power bank (in-000010) and no charger (in-000024). The Giza compound has no A3 card, ruler or clips, and the nearest stationery shop needs an Uber (in-000462). Assembly at his home was not possible on Oct 7 (in-001032). He uses an iPhone (iOS screenshots, file-000039 and file-000720), the DiDi app (Flex, Wasalny and Tayaran options), inDrive (file-000362) and Uber (in-000513), plus WhatsApp (in-000232). He made supplier phone calls well: two shops within 15 minutes on Oct 1 (in-000022), Metanoia, PCBZone, Electrolik, Most, Lampatronics and Panatek on Oct 4-6 (in-000203, in-000220, in-000230, in-000335, in-000470, in-000698). He photographs product pages and invoices clearly (file-000105, file-000134, file-000625). Limits: he could not get a shop's location from Google Maps and asked the shop to send it (in-000309, in-000341). He could not find the 'Confirm I won't pay' button (in-000754, in-000761). About half his bot commands were malformed (see reporting.payment_reporting).
worker-a.travel_behaviour: Modes: ride-hailing cars only. He used DiDi (file-000039, file-000720, file-001139) and inDrive (file-000362) and mentioned an Uber problem (in-000513). No public transport appears in the record. On Oct 7 parts reached him by the technician's courier (in-001023, in-001063). Asking before an overrun was mixed. Oct 1: yes. He sent the 143 EGP one-way quote against a 100 EGP cap before leaving (in-000040, then the top-up in out-000047), and sent the 210 EGP return quote before paying (in-000156, in-000161, spend-000163). Oct 4: no. The PCBZone trip cost 379 against a 300 cap (119 out, 260 back), and he reported it only the next day and on Oct 7 (in-000435, in-001015, spend-001034; ledger D04-04). Oct 5: he sent quotes before leaving (in-000482, in-000485) but never reported actual fares on spend-000487. Oct 6: he sent quotes first (in-000721) and stayed within the 900 cap at 865 (in-000922, in-000929). He chose Wasalny at 417.80 over Flex at 346.80 with the same 15:21 drop-off (file-000720) 'to arrive faster and more comfortably' (in-000725), although Seb had preferred Flex at equal time (out-000723). Oct 7: he sent a 45.90/41.85 quote, then paid 45 with no reservation while Seb had 0 EGP free (in-001140, in-001183; ledger D5-08). Lateness: he warned he might be 15 minutes late (in-000051) and arrived about 30 minutes after the 15:11 ETA (ledger D1-04). On Oct 5 an Uber problem delayed his departure 35 minutes (in-000513; ledger D05-05), and a 47-minute quote became about 90 minutes in traffic (in-000572; ledger D05-08). On Oct 6 he arrived about 40 minutes after the app ETA (in-000764, in-000783; ledger D06-05).

comprehension.handles_simple_logistics: Good. He calls and messages suppliers on his own, relays answers in one or two lines (in-000022, in-000203, in-000470), sends fare screenshots before trips (in-000040, in-000482), and plans around a shop with no signal by asking for the exact buy list and the earlier invoice (in-000520, in-000532). He asks yes/no permission at decision points: go to the branch? another shop? go there? buy there? (in-000034, in-000110, in-000282, in-000477). Weak spots: he could not get a location pin from Google Maps (in-000309, in-000341). He relays supplier claims without probing, for example the board being '5V, Type-C' by phone, which was wrong at the shop (in-000022, in-000123; ledger D1-02), and Panatek's 'no shipping' (in-000721; ledger D06-04).
comprehension.technical_concepts: LED head: on Oct 4 he took Seb's module photo for the finished product to be fabricated (in-000209). Seb's text fixed this: 'the photo is only the LED part; the technician returns LED + wire + USB plug, insulated and tested' (out-000214), followed by a diagram link to forward to the shop (out-000227, out-000234). Voltage and cable: he thought the converter cable went 12V to 5V (in-000321). Seb's one-line correction fixed it: USB 5V in, 12V out to the module (out-000324). Connector: he relayed 'not USB, it's Type-C' (in-000022), Seb explained that Type-C is USB (out-000025), and at the shop he reported the board had no connector (in-000123). Folding: not his task. He never handled wiring. The bot mechanics needed copyable single-line commands (out-000716 then in-000717; out-001036 then in-001042 to in-001051).

language.register: Colloquial Egyptian Arabic, polite and relaxed ('بص', 'متقلقش', 'ماشي', 'تمام'). He greets Seb at shift start (in-000429, in-000644 'صباح الخير يا سيب', in-000899). He frames choices as yes/no questions with 'هل … ؟' (in-000034, in-000110, in-000477). He writes English tech words in Latin script: usb, tybe C, description, Pcb, most, pcb zone (in-000022, in-000132, in-000282, in-000315, in-000341). Many typos: مناح for متاح, ليذات for ليدات (in-000022), معنيش for معنديش (in-000010), حاهز for جاهز (in-000698), تاميد for تأكيد (in-000754), هلاص for خلاص (in-000572), الحد for الأحد (in-001030). He mixes Arabic-Indic and Western digits. No emoji.
language.typical_length: Short. Median 7 words, mean 8.6, p90 17, max 44 (in-000435). About 20% of text messages are 3 words or fewer. 14 of 136 messages carry an image, 6 of them without a caption (in-000106, in-001086). Numbers often come alone as a fare caption ('110', '335', '343': in-000363, in-000482, in-000485). He sends 21-46 messages a shift (46 on Oct 7, mostly /paid work).

message_categories.method: One primary label per chat message from the day core files. Messages tagged HIDDEN-FROM-SEB (/budget, /log and their replies) are excluded. Seb labels: keyword rules on the opening of each message plus manual overrides on about 190 messages after reading. Counts are approximate (+/- a few per type), because many Seb messages combine an ask, a cap and a reminder. Worker labels: assigned by hand to all 136 worker-a and 216 worker-b messages. 'Off-shift' covers Seb messages outside shift hours, including Oct 2-3, which the Oct 1 file contains.

seb_instruction_types.type: status check: where are you, ETA, result, what you have with you
ask a supplier, technician or venue (phone, WhatsApp or in person), usually with an exact script
payment reporting: actual amount, /paid, receipt, confirm won't-pay
off-shift plan or next-shift update (no reply needed)
assembly, mounting, testing or folding step
buy one specific item or service within an EGP cap
go to a place: travel approved within an EGP cap, with conditions
bot reply to a worker command
stop, wait, stay put, or start returning before shift end
delivery and meeting planning (private address handling, public points)
relay news about the other worker or the plan for later
technical explanation, diagram or correction of a misunderstanding
supplier address, map link, phone number or invoice data on request
copyable /paid line for the worker to resend

location, travel, ETA or timing status
asks what to do next or whether to go or buy
photo without caption (item, receipt, map, location)
bot command attempt or cancellation attempt

asks for information: location, number, plan, invoice, exact list
payment amount, receipt or reconciliation in chat
fare quote before booking (screenshot or number)
concept check on a technical point
